notes: Row heading over the measured effect of the stack you would be taking. Read while a level-up card is up, or while hovering a hexagon in the hive. Two words at most — it sits in a 9-character column beside the measurement.

Row heading over the running total across the stacks already held ("+112% fire rate"). Has to read as "where you are now" against the row above it, which is "what one more buys". Same 9-character column.
Row heading over what the ability has actually done this run — damage, kills, or times it went off. Same 9-character column.
Unit after a damage figure in that row: "412.1k ___". One word.
Unit after a kill count: "380 ___". One word, and it has to work at 1 as well as at 380.
Unit after a count of times a damageless ability went off — a beluga bubble, a charm, a freeze, a net haul: "7 ___". One word, same 1-and-many problem.
Replaces the whole "next" row on a stack that has hit its maxStacks. Says "there is no next one", not "this is broken". One or two words.

Fills the "this run" row when the ledger has a zero for an ability the player IS holding. It is a real fact and the tip says it out loud rather than hiding the row — so it should read as an honest nothing, not as an error. Two or three words.

The section heading over the fin split in the run summary's weapons breakdown, with a damage figure beside it. Sits under the same eye as "Weapons" and "What killed you", so it wants their register — one or two words naming the pair of flippers as a source of damage.

The heading over the score screen's rail on a run with NO kill shots — the rail is still there holding the hive of upgrades, and Ethan's "Kill shots" would be the screen getting a fact wrong about the run. Two or three words, same size as "Kill shots".
The screen reader's name for the hexagon block on that rail, read aloud in place of a picture. Has to say what the thing IS and that pressing it opens it. A short phrase, not a sentence.
The accessible name on the ✕ that shuts the full-screen build sheet. Never seen — read aloud. Matches how the kill-shot sheet's own close button is named.

What the share/save row says after the DESKTOP shell saved through a real file dialog — the player chose where it went, so "Saved to your downloads" (the phone wording, beside this one) would be a guess and usually wrong. Two or three words, same voice as "Shared" and "Nothing to share".
The name of the clap action in the key-rebinding list, beside "Charge strike" and "Pause". What the player DOES, two words at most; the hardware hint ("X / Square") is separate and already written.
Option name in the Boost meter picker. Already yours — here because its three options belong in one place.
Option name in the Boost meter picker. Already yours — here because its three options belong in one place.
The third option in the Boost meter picker, meaning BOTH of the two above are drawn at once. It is also the default. One or two words, matching the register of the two beside it.
The pause-menu row that sets how much a hovered upgrade tells you. Fits one line at 375px wide, so two or three words.
The grey line under that row. One short sentence saying what the setting changes, in the voice of the hints beside it ("How the strike fuel is drawn").
First of three option names. Means no tip anywhere — the level-up cards read as name and desc and nothing else. One word.
Second option: the name, and what the stack you are being offered does. The question at the moment of a pick, nothing else. One word.
Third option and the default: adds the running total across the stacks held and what the ability has done this run. One word.

Which flipper the Flippers Up! card is about to feed, appended to the card's title — the one thing {effect} cannot measure. Two words at most, and it fills the slot a stack number fills on every other card.
The other flipper, same slot. The pair has to read as a pair; whichever way "left" is written, this is its twin.

Heading over the strip of accessories on the main menu — the drawer of things the seal can wear. Two words at most; it sits above a row of small tiles on a screen that already has Play on it, so it has to name the drawer without competing with the buttons.
Shown in the drawer when the player has unlocked nothing yet. Has to read as "there will be things here" rather than as an error. One short sentence, five or six words.
The first tile in the drawer: wearing nothing. Sits beside the hat and the glasses as an equal choice, so it needs a name rather than a dash. One or two words.
The captain's cap, as the player sees it on its tile and when it is put on. Two words at most — the tiles are small and the name sits under the picture.
The pixel sunglasses, same tile. Two or three words; it is the funnier of the two and the drawer is where the joke lands.

A bowler hat with a pair of brass goggles strapped to the band, on its tile and when it goes on. Two words at most — the tiles are 64px wide and the name wraps to two lines if it runs long. It sits in a row beside the other two hats, so the three have to be tellable apart by name alone.
The pirate tricorn — three-cornered, worn point forward. Same tile, same two-word ceiling. The most obviously costume-y thing in the drawer.
A brown felt fedora, brim turned down at the front. Same tile. Two words at most, and it has to read as a different hat from the other two rather than as a third word for "hat".

Round spectacles in thick wooden frames — reading glasses rather than shades. Two or three words; it shares the row with two pairs of sunglasses, so the name is what says these are the ones you can see through.
Gold-wire aviators with a green tint. Same tile, two words at most.

Small round gold wire frames with near-black lenses. Same tile. Two or three words, and it has to be distinguishable from the aviators, which are also gold wire — the difference the player sees is round versus teardrop, and small versus wide.
